title: Book One · Chapter 113: Six Books on a Dry Table
story:
After the morning lessons, Miss Wu clears some table space. It is for the damp exercise books.

Mr Qiu comes with Mum to ask. He waits for Miss Wu to show him a place. She points to a clear table in the store room. It is just beside the classroom. Then he puts his tray down. The room has a dry window and no leaking roof.

“These have no writing in them,” he says. “They are new stock. Six books.”

Miss Wu checks the corners. She can offer the table for a few days. She cannot turn her whole classroom into a store. Mr Qiu thanks her and agrees to come back to check them.

Ronan expected terrible books. They look mostly ordinary. He gently touches the corner of one book. The corner feels soft under his fingers.

Miss Wu asks the children to wash and dry their hands first. “Support a book from below,” she says. They must not lift it by a wet page. They lay the six books apart on the table. Miss Wu points to spaces for the clean dry paper. It goes between the damp parts.

“No pulling stuck pages,” she says. “Call me if they do not come apart easily.”

Leo finds two pages. They are stuck together. He leaves them and raises his hand. He must go slowly with the wet pages.

Mei makes six small number cards. Ronan checks the numbers aloud while she puts one beside each book. They write Mr Qiu's name on a separate label for the table. Nothing goes into anyone's school bag.

When the rain eases, Miss Wu opens the window a little. She checks it again. Then she leaves the room. The children may help when she is there. They may not use heat to dry the books. They must not take them home to dry faster.

Ronan wants the corner to become dry while he watches. It stays dark.

“We have a reading lesson,” Miss Wu says.

“Can I check after?”

“When I can come with you.”

He goes back to his desk. The story is about a letter. A person is waiting for it. He is still thinking about the books next door. He has to read the first line twice.

At lunch, Leo asks about the books. Will the children get to keep the ones they save?

“They are Mr Qiu's,” Ronan says.

“I know. He may offer them to us.”

“He did not offer them.”

Leo eats another bite. “Fair enough.”

After the last lesson, Miss Wu lets them check again. Two corners feel less soft. Four are still quite damp. She changes some of the clean paper herself. She leaves the books supported on the table.

Ronan draws six little rectangles in his notebook. “May I mark these two books?” he asks. “They feel better.” “Write today's result,” Miss Wu says. “An adult must check the books. The pages need to be dry. Then Mr Qiu can choose a day to collect them.”

He writes LESS DAMP beside two. He does not write SAVED. The books are not dry yet. LESS DAMP tells the result.

On the way home, “How many books were there?” Mum asks. “There were six books,” he says. Two felt less damp. Four were still quite wet. She listens all the way to the gate.

Mrs Lan's front room still holds the dry crates. Ronan does not open them to compare. One list is for stock in the crates. Another is for the books at school. Those books are drying there. He keeps his own notebook in his room. His notebook has a list of Mr Qiu's things. It does not give Ronan permission to move them. He must still ask Mr Qiu first.
studyGuide:
## 重点表达

- support a book from below＝从底部托住书
- come apart＝分开
- today's result＝今天的结果
- less damp＝没那么潮

额外情节词（不要求本章全部记住）：stuck together＝粘连；stock＝存货；notebook＝笔记本。

## 读句提示

**How many books were there?**

那里／一共有／多少本书？完整直接问句。

## 理解问题

1. 孩子们怎样帮助晾书，又遵守哪些边界？
2. “没那么潮”为什么比“救好了”更准确？
